 Intensify dengue prevention efforts
 Says PM; govt mulls dengue vaccine trials 
 Published : 14 October 2026
 • 
 Updated : 14 October 2026, 03:44
 • 
 DISEASE
 SHARE 
 Staff Correspondent 
 Prime Minister Tarique Rahman yesterday directed the authorities to intensify public awareness campaigns and strengthen coordination among government agencies to contain dengue, which has claimed 316 lives and hospitalised 1,03,396 people so far this year.
 He issued the directives at a meeting on dengue prevention and control at the Cabinet Division in the Secretariat, said PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 The prime minister said the next few months would be crucial for controlling dengue and called for stronger preventive measures, particularly in areas reporting higher infection rates.
 He directed the authorities to arrange regular loudspeaker announcements in neighbourhoods and include dengue prevention messages in Juma prayer sermons.
 The meeting also decided to ensure cleanliness at government residential quarters and hospital premises.
 Meanwhile, the government will consult experts on whether to conduct clinical trials of dengue vaccines vin Bangladesh or assess existing research before considering their use, State Minister for Health Dr MA Muhit said yesterday.
 Speaking to reporters after a seminar on mental health at Bangla Academy, he said the issue was discussed at the meeting with the prime minister.
 “Before approving a vaccine, we need scientific data and must consult experts to understand how it will work for our population,” he said.
 Muhit said several dengue vaccine candidates were at different stages of development internationally, while India had recently approved one for private-sector use.
 The government is also considering trials of a Japanese mosquito-control technology alongside conventional preventive measures.
 Muhit said the two Dhaka city corporations would establish fever clinics at different locations across the capital to facilitate prompt dengue testing.
 He advised people with fever to seek medical attention at hospitals or the clinics rather than rely on pharmacies or unqualified practitioners.
 Around 2,000 doctors, including physicians at medical college and district hospitals, received refresher training on dengue management last month, he said.
 Muhit also said the government had begun recruiting 5,000 doctors, planned to recruit 2,500 nurses soon and initiated discussions on recruiting medical technologists to address staff shortages in public hospitals.
